prompt:
Draft a procedure for communication of OH&S information at a large construction project with multiple subcontractors. Include internal communication (toolbox talks, safety alerts, notice boards), external communication (regulator, public, emergency services), consultation mechanisms, and documentation requirements. Address language barriers and literacy levels. Align with ISO 45001 clause 7.4.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "OH&S INFORMATION COMMUNICATION PROCEDURE FOR LARGE CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS

1. PURPOSE
This procedure establishes a standardized framework for the communication of Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) information across all levels of a large construction project involving multiple subcontractors. It ensures compliance with ISO 45001 Clause 7.4 by promoting effective internal and external communication, meaningful consultation, and accessible documentation, while addressing language barriers and varying literacy levels.

2. SCOPE
Applies to all project personnel, including direct employees, subcontractors, suppliers, visitors, regulators, emergency services, and the public. Covers all project phases: mobilization, construction, and demobilization.

3. RESPONSIBILITIES
- Project Safety Manager: Oversees implementation, ensures compliance, and maintains documentation.
- Site Supervisors: Conduct toolbox talks, distribute alerts, and ensure understanding.
- Subcontractor Safety Representatives: Facilitate communication within their teams and report barriers.
- HR & Training Team: Provide translation, visual aids, and literacy support.
- Public Relations Officer: Manages external communications with regulators and the public.

4. INTERNAL COMMUNICATION
4.1 Toolbox Talks
- Conducted daily or before high-risk tasks by site supervisors.
- Delivered in the primary language of the workforce and at least one additional common language (e.g., English, Spanish, Tagalog).
- Use pictograms, videos, and physical demonstrations to overcome literacy barriers.
- Attendance recorded digitally via mobile app with biometric or ID tag verification.
- All talks archived in the OH&S Management System.

4.2 Safety Alerts
- Issued immediately for emerging hazards (e.g., structural instability, chemical spill).
- Distributed via SMS, mobile app push notifications, and printed posters in multiple languages.
- Posted on all site notice boards with icons and color coding (red = urgent, yellow = caution).
- Alerts reviewed and acknowledged by all subcontractor team leaders within 1 hour.

4.3 Notice Boards
- Located at all site entrances, break areas, and accommodation zones.
- Content includes: daily safety messages, incident reports (anonymized), upcoming training, and emergency contacts.
- All text translated into top 5 languages spoken on site (determined by workforce survey).
- Visuals dominate: diagrams, flowcharts, and photos with minimal text.
- Updated daily by Safety Officer.

5. EXTERNAL COMMUNICATION
5.1 Regulators
- Submit monthly OH&S performance reports via approved digital portal.
- Notify regulators within 1 hour of any reportable incident (injury, fatality, near miss).
- Maintain open line of communication via designated Safety Manager contact.

5.2 Public
- Publish weekly safety updates on project website and community noticeboards.
- Use simple language, infographics, and multilingual summaries.
- Host quarterly community safety forums with interpreters.
- Respond to public inquiries within 24 hours.

5.3 Emergency Services
- Provide emergency response plans (ERP) in digital and printed formats to local fire, police, and EMS.
- Conduct joint drills biannually with emergency services.
- Share site maps, hazard locations, and contact lists in plain language and visual format.

6. CONSULTATION MECHANISMS
- Weekly Safety Committee meetings: Include representatives from each major subcontractor, union (if applicable), and worker volunteers.
- Anonymous feedback channels: Digital kiosks, SMS hotline, and suggestion boxes in multiple languages.
- Worker representatives elected by peer vote; trained in OH&S communication and ISO 45001 requirements.
- All feedback logged, responded to within 48 hours, and outcomes communicated via notice boards and app.

7. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
- All communication records (toolbox talk logs, alert distributions, consultation minutes) stored in centralized cloud-based OH&S Management System.
- Documents retained for minimum 5 years or as required by local law.
- All documents available in digital and printed formats.
- Version control applied; outdated materials archived and removed from notice boards.
- Audit trails for all communications (who sent, when, to whom, acknowledgments).

8. ADDRESSING LANGUAGE BARRIERS AND LITERACY LEVELS
- All written materials use simple vocabulary, short sentences, and active voice.
- Mandatory use of universally recognized safety symbols (ISO 3864 compliant).
- On-site interpreters available during high-risk operations and safety meetings.
- Multilingual safety ambassadors (trained workers) assigned to each language group.
- Training materials available as audio recordings and video demonstrations.
- Literacy assessments conducted during onboarding; tailored support provided.

9. REVIEW AND IMPROVEMENT
- This procedure reviewed annually or after any major incident.
- Feedback from workers and subcontractors used to update content and delivery methods.
- Compliance audited quarterly against ISO 45001 Clause 7.4.

10. REFERENCES
- ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.4
- OSHA 1926.21 – Safety Training and Education
- Local OH&S Legislation

Approved by: [Project Director]
Effective Date: [Date]
